title: Eleven Seconds
summary: A second Big Bear recording opens with Steve Lee freestyling over Money Mark's music, then returns to the Lee brothers' running comparison. The first sustained discussion revisits Bobby Lee and Kalilah's Tinder origin. Kalilah says Bobby deleted Tinder during her hospitalization but later reinstalled it, accumulated matches and was discovered using it in Vancouver. Bobby says he restored it in Houston to demonstrate the app and forgot to remove it. The room distinguishes curiosity and fantasy from cheating, while also naming matches, swiping, a reported shoulder check and a recurring habit of defending Bobby. Kalilah then counters idealized relationship advice with the domestic reality of a five-year balcony urine container. The title comes from her description of Bobby's brief burst of rapid sex followed by a forehead kiss. That opens a long, explicit but presented-as-consensual discussion of sexual noises, awkwardness, death/humiliation play and intricate fantasy. The record preserves this material without treating statements inside roleplay as admissions. It separately flags adult age-regression, incest, death and minor-coded fantasies, and it corrects but does not endorse the room's loose clinical terminology. A discussion of Elliot Rodger and Seung-Hui Cho mixes public mass killings, racial slurs, stereotypes, anti-bullying fear and David's counterfactual claim that another life path could have led him toward Columbine-like violence; the room explicitly says murder is wrong, and the record does not convert the counterfactual into a present threat. Episode 134's forced genital-touch event is recalled and remains classified as nonconsensual. The group then reveals shared access to Critter's social accounts, discovers a Tinder impersonator using his photos, and creates a collective profile. Those facts are retained while private operators, matches, workers and discoverability mechanics are restricted. The masturbation challenge, Macau proposal, strip-club stories, Asa Akira's book tour, sibling support and pressure on Bobby and Kalilah to stay overnight all continue prior threads. Near the end, the cast proposes replacement racial and homophobic code words. The source speech and its premise remain uncensored, but the invented labels are documented as an episode-specific racist-comedy bit rather than adopted as archival categories. The formal ending is followed by a music session; decoder loops at the opening and during the jam are marked indistinct instead of rendered as dialogue. No named line-level transcript is published because held-out speaker validation remains insufficient.
source_notes: The cleaner removes 176 records for a net 154-segment reduction. Most are empty records or one-token decoder loops at the opening and during the closing jam; readable musical material remains represented with uncertainty markers.

Accept Asa Akira, David Choe, DVDASA, Pamela Adlon and the second David Choe normalization. Reject Bobby Namba to Bobby Hundreds, all three health-podcast semantic rewrites, and Sizzler to Twizzler. Public names still do not authorize turn-level speaker labels.
The title is explicitly explained as roughly eleven seconds of rapid intercourse followed by a forehead kiss. This is separate from the forced-touch consent event carried over from Episode 134.

The couple's Tinder account is not described as passive: the episode reports right-swiping and matches. It still does not establish physical cheating, and Kalilah says she did not treat the incident as a major fight.
Reported death, humiliation, incest and age-regression scenarios are described as consensual adult fantasy. Claims spoken inside the fantasy are not treated as admissions of real conduct.

The room's pedophilia/hebephilia definitions are incomplete conversational claims, not clinical or legal guidance. References to child actors and minor-coded roleplay require warning without erasing the material.
Elliot Rodger and Seung-Hui Cho are public perpetrators discussed imprecisely. Historical facts require source verification before publication beyond this episode map.

The collective Tinder profile and proposed female-fan Ranch contest are historical stunts/proposals. The archive does not republish methods that facilitate private-person discovery or renewed solicitation.
The racial-code exercise is retained as source content but its invented terms are not used to classify people, themes or speakers elsewhere in the corpus.
The show signs off around 1:05:22 and continues into a jam/outro. The later sparse transcript is not evidence of a missing episode ending.
speaker_policy: Episode metadata may name explicitly introduced or unmistakably public participants including David Choe, Asa Akira, Bobby Lee, Kalilah, Money Mark and Steve Lee. Zero independently validated turns and zero identity windows prohibit assigning any individual line to them or to Critter, Valentin, Bill Poon or other room participants.
